problem_statement: Unpacking a DNS name into a fixed-size buffer does not correctly enforce the destination buffer's capacity. dns_unpack_name() copies each label of an encoded DNS name into a destination net_buf, separating labels with dots and terminating with a NUL byte. When the assembled name would not fit in the destination buffer (for example a query name built from several 63-byte labels whose combined length, plus dot separators and the terminating NUL, exceeds the buffer size), the function must reject it and return an error instead of writing past the buffer. Before the fix, very long names that exceed the buffer capacity are accepted and overflow the buffer rather than being rejected.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/net/lib/dns_resolve -s tests/net/lib/dns_resolve/net.dns.resolve -s net.dns.resolve -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The bug and high-level requirement are described, but the tests rely on exact error and success return semantics that can be added to the statement without revealing the implementation.

problems.detail: The statement says the function must return an error, but the hidden tests require the specific error code -EMSGSIZE.

The hidden tests also require that a name exactly filling the buffer is accepted and that successful unpacking continues to return the unpacked name length excluding the terminating NUL; the statement does not state these public behaviours explicitly.

problem_statement_fixed:
Unpacking a DNS name into a fixed-size buffer does not correctly enforce the destination buffer's capacity. dns_unpack_name() copies each label of an encoded DNS name into a destination net_buf, separating labels with dots and terminating with a NUL byte. When the assembled name would not fit in the destination buffer (for example a query name built from several 63-byte labels whose combined length, plus dot separators and the terminating NUL, exceeds the buffer size), the function must reject it instead of writing past the buffer. Before the fix, very long names that exceed the buffer capacity are accepted and overflow the buffer rather than being rejected.

When unpacking fails for a size or length reason, dns_unpack_name() must return -EMSGSIZE. A name that exactly fills the buffer, including the dot separators and the terminating NUL, must still be accepted. For names that fit, dns_unpack_name() must continue to return the length of the assembled name excluding the terminating NUL and must preserve its existing behavior for valid names and for the end_of_label pointer.
